messages:
maria: Quick ask — can we add a lightweight 'preview' + 'replay' flow to deploy-bot? For the sprint: need fast release-note previews, a dry-run that generates a rollback script, and a change-window calendar hint. Simple UX, low friction.

sam: +1. I think 3 small commands will cover it:
- `/deploy preview --range <commit-range> --format short` => auto-aggregate commits, labels, owners
- `/deploy replay --preview-id <id> --dryrun` => run the pipeline against staging reproducing the same steps and produce rollback.sh
- `/deploy schedule-window --start <iso> --end <iso> --tz <tz>` => annotate the deploy with a change window (syncs to calendar)

sam: provisional CLI examples:
```
# preview release notes
/deploy preview --range HEAD~20..HEAD --format short

# replay a preview id and ask for rollback script
/deploy replay --preview-id p-2026-03-18-1234 --dryrun --annotate-rollbacks

# schedule change window
/deploy schedule-window --start 2026-03-19T22:00Z --end 2026-03-20T02:00Z --tz UTC
```

deploy-bot: preview created p-2026-03-18-1234 — https://deploy.redwood.internal/previews/p-2026-03-18-1234 :eyes:

akshay: two questions: 1) How do we ensure previews don't leak secrets? 2) When the replay produces rollback.sh, is it deterministic and reviewed automatically?

sam: Good calls.
1) previews/replays run in an isolated k8s namespace with env scrubbers and no customer keys. Artifacts are short-lived (TTL 24h) and stored encrypted.
2) rollback.sh is generated from the same manifest diffs and a policy table. We can include metadata and a confidence score. Example output:
```
# rollback.sh (generated)
#!/bin/bash
# rollback to v1.2.14
kubectl set image deployment/web web=image:v1.2.14 --namespace prod
kubectl rollout status deployment/web --namespace prod
# note: confirm db migration rollback manually
```

jen: Product: please add a small 'release-note blurb' field in preview so PMs can edit before publish. Also for change windows, calendar invite auto-generated + include slack reminders.

alex: Implementation note — store previews in s3 under previews/<id>/artifact.json and attach a short signed url. Add `replay --from s3://...` to allow replaying old previews.

maria: This looks great. Sam — can you slot a 1hr pairing this week to prototype the preview command? I'd like a demo for QA before end of sprint. Tag me when ready.

deploy-bot: scheduled job created: prototype-demo -> @sam @maria on 2026-03-19T15:00Z :calendar:

sam: I'll take it. Will post an initial PR with the preview aggregator and a small UI for the preview page. Thanks all :sparkles:
